subject: Mutual Action Plan: unit economics verification & close timeline
snippet: Quick alignment on tokens/$, caching and batching assumptions for the MAP; confirm sim results and solidify close date.

Subject: Pre-MAP: unit econ inputs & timeline

Hey Rishi / Priyom —

Thanks for the run-through yesterday. Before we lock the MAP, finance wants a short verification of the unit economics assumptions so the CFO can sign off. High level asks: tokens/$ sensitivity (best/expected/worst), any caching/prefix reuse assumptions that materially change cost, and whether batching prefetched tokens is on the roadmap for the pilot.

We also need a target close date (they're aiming for EoQ, so ~Sep 30). Can you share a short checklist and any sims you can run quickly?

Appreciate it —
Brad

Attachments: none
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pre-MAP: unit econ inputs & timeline

Brad —

Thanks — high level first pass below, and attaching a concise deck + sims. I kept it intentionally short so you can circulate to finance. Key points: 

1) Tokens/$ sensitivity (pilot chat workload):
   - Best case (prefetch + high reuse): ~14k tokens / $1 (quantized config + 8-bit kernels)
   - Expected (moderate reuse, batching enabled, prefix cache hit ~20%): ~6.5k tokens / $1
   - Worst case (no cache, tail-heavy prompts): ~2.2k tokens / $1

2) Caching assumptions:
   - Prefix KV caching assumed for session-based reuse; we conservatively model 15–25% cache hit for discovery flows, 35–45% for template-driven flows.
   - Cache warmup windows: 5–15 minutes depending on traffic burstiness.

3) Batching & prefetching:
   - We recommend small continuous batching (micro-batches of 4–8) for low-latency pathways and larger batch windows for async jobs.
   - Prefetching top-k prompts for templated responses is planned for pilot week 2; material savings in best/expected scenarios.

4) Risks / gating for MAP close:
   - If cache hit <10% and we see long tail prompts, economic delta may push expected tokens/$ down ~30–50%.
   - Quantization variants (4-bit) need perf validation on their prompt lengths to ensure quality SLA.

Deliverables this week (plan):
- Priyom: run traffic sims with three traffic profiles (template-heavy, mixed, exploratory) and attach CSV with per-scenario tokens/$ (due 9/13).
- Neha: compile a one-page note on any SLAs/quality tradeoffs for quantized models (due 9/14).
- I will produce a one-page MAP cost appendix and update the MAP timeline (due 9/13).

Target close: Sep 30 is achievable if sims confirm expected tokens/$ and legal procurement steps stay on track.

Attaching: unit-econ-deck-v2.pdf and token-sim-results.csv (prelim).

Thanks —
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra

Team / Brad —

Quick update: I ran the three traffic sims against the expected pilot prompt distribution. Summary (see attached CSV for numbers):

- Template-heavy: tokens/$ = 11,800 (cache hit ~42%, micro-batching applied)
- Mixed: tokens/$ = 6,200 (cache hit ~22%, batching 4–6)
- Exploratory: tokens/$ = 2,600 (cache hit ~8%, batching less effective)

Notes: the CSV includes per-request token breakdown, batching windows simulated, and sensitivity to quantization step from 8-bit -> 4-bit (quality drop risk flagged). Prefetching templated prompts (enabled in sim) accounts for the bulk of uplift in template-heavy flows.

Action items I recommend we include in the MAP appendix:
- Pilot acceptance criteria: Mixed profile tokens/$ >= 5.5k (we're at 6.2k)
- Conditional optimization bets: enable prefetch + prefix cache tuning week 2; measure actual cache hit on day 3 and adjust SLO.
- Fallback plan: if mixed profile <5k on prod day 1, roll to dedicated capacity with pre-agreed spend cap and fallback model variant with lower token costs.

I'll convert the CSV into one chart for the MAP appendix by EOD 9/13.

—Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Rishi / Priyom / Neha —

This is really helpful, thanks. I circulated the deck and the sims to our finance and product leads. A couple quick asks before we file the MAP: 

- Can you add a short line in the MAP appendix that lists the specific runtime config used for each row in the CSV (model variant, quantization, batch window, cache enabled true/false)? Finance wants the knobs tied to the numbers.
- Legal needs confirmation that enabling prefetch doesn't change PII handling (we treat prefetch prompts as derived from customer templates). Neha — can you confirm; if yes we can mark it as no-change, otherwise we need a short mitigation plan.

Assuming those two items are clear, we are OK to sign the MAP and target a Sep 30 close with a go-live pilot week of Oct 11. Would you also add a single-line note that the fallback plan includes a capped dedicated pool option if tokens/$ drop below the mixed-profile acceptance threshold?

If you can get the two clarifications by end-of-day tomorrow (9/16), I can route to CFO.

Thanks —
Brad
